newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo to cut Lonrho stake to under 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Anglo to cut Lonrho stake to under 10 percent.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Corp., under pressure from the European Commission, has backed down and agreed to cut its stake in Lonrho Plc to under 10 percent, sources close to Anglo said Friday.
The sources said Anglo will settle its dispute with the Commission over its 25.8 percent stake in Lonrho by reducing the stake over two years.

The EU has said Anglo's stake in Lonrho -- which has substantial interest in two South African platinum mines -- would put control of the world's platinum industry in the hands of Anglo and another South African mining house, Gencor Ltd.
The Commission said in February that Anglo's shareholding in Lonrho had the possibility of the South African conglomerate exercising decisive influence over Lonrho.
The sources said the Commission felt that "platinum was a highly sensitive matter" and such harsh measures were necessary for policy reasons.
The settlement would see the remainder of Anglo's stake, around 17 percent, placed in a voting trust to be sold off under supervision of the Commission.

Analysts have said that Anglo's main aim in buying the 18 percent stake in Lonrho of the company's former Chief Executive Dieter Bock, was to gain Lonrho's 33.6 percent stake in Ashanti Goldfields Co.
The sources said the settlement would not affect any future Anglo plans to pursue Lonrho's other interests in sugar, coal or Ashanti.
Anglo was warned against taking control of Lonrho a year ago, when the Commission blocked the proposed merger of Gencor's platinum interests with that of Lonrho.
Lonrho owns around 73 percent of Eastern and Western Platinum -- its own platinum division -- with 23 percent held by Gencor.
Anglo's platinum division, Anglo American Platinum Corp. of South Africa Ltd produces around 38 percent of the world's newly-mined platinum.
